RESULTS SUMMARY BY FUEL C.1 BIODIESEL (BD) C.1.1 Production Pathways and Cost In this study, we examine the biodiesel (BD) pathway using soybean oil and used cooking oil (UCO) through commercially available transesterification technology. As illustrated in Figure 3-1, the modeled minimum fuel selling price (MFSP) for BD derived from soybean oil is $3.51 per diesel gallon equivalent (DGE), with approximately 85% of this cost attributed to feedstock. When substituting soybean oil for the less-expensive UCO, the feedstock contribution to the MFSP decreases by about $1.12/DGE. However, capital expenditures (CAPEX) and fixed operating costs increase by $0.75/DGE and $0.95/DGE, respectively, because the smaller plant scale is limited by UCO availability. Overall, the modeled MFSP for a 44-million -lb/year UCO BD plant is approximately $0.60/DGE higher than that of a typical soybean oil BD plant with an annual production capacity of 220 million lb. In addition, the MFSP of BD from UCO is subject to higher uncertainties because the market price of UCO varies more significantly. C.1.2 Lifecycle Emissions BD from soybean oil and UCO generate 27 and 15 g CO e/MJ. This is equivalent to 69% and 83% 2 emission reductions compared to conventional diesel use in freight rail. Because UCO is the waste feedstock, the feedstock phase only includes UCO collection and transport to the biorefinery facility. In contrast, the feedstock phase for soybean oil includes soybean farming, soybean oil refinery, transportation and distribution stages. It is worth noting that land use change emission also contributes 9.3 g CO e/MJ to BD from the soybean oil pathway, which is equivalent to 34% 2 of its total lifecycle emissions. The land use change emissions are derived from Carbon Calculator for Land Use and Land Management Change from Biofuels Production (CCLUB) model (Argonne, 2020). C.2 RENEWABLE DIESEL (RD) C.2.1 Production Pathways and Cost For RD pathways, we examine the commercially available HEFA technology using soybean oil and UCO, along with emerging RD technologies such as HTL converting wet wastes. We also studied RD production from woody biomass with CFP and FT technologies. The MFSPs for these six RD pathways range from $3.47 to $4.65 per DGE.
